lanes.name: Baron lane
lanes.intro: Four kinds of Baron laner. These calls match the site's Baron matchup data: ranged tops won every listed matchup against juggernauts, and juggernauts beat tanks in most.

types.name: Ranged tops
types.identity: Kite melee champions and poke them off the wave. Weak once a melee champion gets on top of them.
types.winCondition: Poke every time the enemy walks up to farm, and keep the wave near your side so they have to walk through your damage.

types.name: Skirmishers
types.identity: Mobile duelists with dashes, sustain or true damage. Strongest in 1v1s and side lanes.
types.winCondition: Win short trades on cooldowns, then split-push and duel anyone who comes to stop you.

types.name: Juggernauts
types.identity: Slow, tanky damage dealers with no real dash. Win any long fight they can force.
types.winCondition: Make the enemy fight you in melee range for a long time: walk them down, freeze the wave and punish every mistake.

types.name: Tanks
types.identity: Survive lane, then engage or peel for the team. They rarely win lane on damage.
types.winCondition: Farm safely, don't feed, and arrive first to team fights and objectives with your ultimate ready.

matchups.why: Juggernauts have no dash, so a ranged top can poke them on every last-hit and walk away before they connect.
matchups.tip: As the juggernaut: give up minions rather than health, keep your gap-closer for when they walk up, and ask for early ganks.

matchups.why: Tanks can't punish poke, so ranged tops take free plates and push them under tower all game.
matchups.tip: As the tank: farm under tower, buy resistances early, and roam with your ultimate once it's up.

matchups.why: Skirmishers with dashes through minions, like Irelia and Yasuo, close the gap; ones without get kited.
matchups.tip: As the ranged top: keep the wave small so there are fewer minions to dash through, and save your escape for their engage.

matchups.why: Tanks can't escape a juggernaut's long fights, and juggernaut damage keeps scaling into their HP.
matchups.tip: As the tank: trade only when their key ability is down, and farm under tower until your resistances come online.

matchups.why: Skirmishers dodge the one ability juggernauts need to land, like Darius's pull or Garen's silence, and win short trades.
matchups.tip: As the juggernaut: hold your crowd control until their dash is down, and freeze the wave so they have to walk up to you.

matchups.why: True and %HP damage skirmishers like Fiora, Gwen and Vayne shred tanks, but crowd-control tanks like Poppy and Malphite stop dash skirmishers cold.
matchups.tip: Check the exact champions: skirmishers with true damage win, dash-reliant ones lose to tanks with dash-stopping CC.

exceptions.name: Poppy
exceptions.text: A tank who beats dash skirmishers: her W stops dashes near her, which shuts down Irelia and Yasuo.

exceptions.name: Fiora
exceptions.text: A skirmisher who beats tanks: her vitals deal true damage based on max HP, so tank HP makes her stronger.

exceptions.name: Mordekaiser
exceptions.text: A juggernaut who wins even more against tanks: his R steals their stats inside his realm.

exceptions.name: Malphite
exceptions.text: A tank who beats auto-attack skirmishers like Jax: his armor and E attack-speed slow cut their damage.

exceptions.name: Irelia
exceptions.text: A skirmisher who beats ranged tops: she dashes through minions to reach them, which breaks the ranged-beats-melee rule.

lanes.name: Dragon lane (marksmen)
lanes.intro: Not every marksman plays the same. Your marksman type decides how hard you trade in lane and when your team should fight.

types.name: Lane bullies
types.identity: Strong in levels 1–5 with high damage or long range. They need to build a lead before scaling marksmen catch up.
types.winCondition: Trade hard early, take plates and the first drakes, then end before the other marksman finishes items.

types.name: Hypercarries
types.identity: Weak early, the strongest damage in the game late. Need farm and time.
types.winCondition: Survive lane, never miss farm, and fight once your core items or stacks are done.

types.name: Utility and poke
types.identity: Long-range poke, slows or roots that help the team more than raw damage does.
types.winCondition: Poke before fights start, and use your crowd control to set up or stop engages.

types.name: All-in skirmishers
types.identity: Short-range marksmen who dash into fights and win close-range brawls with an engage support.
types.winCondition: Pair with an engage support, look for level 2 and 3 all-ins, and snowball off kills.

matchups.why: Lane bullies punish every last-hit while hypercarries are weak, and can end the lane before the hypercarry scales.
matchups.tip: As the hypercarry: farm under tower, give up plates rather than deaths, and ask your jungler to play your side.

matchups.why: Range and early damage punish a short-range marksman before they can get close enough to all-in.
matchups.tip: As the skirmisher: wait for your support's engage instead of walking up, and fight only when the bully has used their escape.

matchups.why: Both are strong early; it comes down to who wins the poke war and whose support controls the lane.
matchups.tip: Play around your support: the lane with the better engage or the better sustain usually wins it.

matchups.why: Even lanes, but utility marksmen fall off late, and a farmed hypercarry out-damages them in every fight.
matchups.tip: As the utility marksman: use your lane lead to take objectives early, before the hypercarry comes online.

matchups.why: Immobile hypercarries can't escape an early all-in, so skirmishers snowball before items matter.
matchups.tip: As the hypercarry: stand behind minions, save your escape for their dash, and play for later fights.

matchups.why: Slows, roots and long-range poke keep skirmishers from getting close enough to all-in.
matchups.tip: As the skirmisher: wait until their crowd control is on cooldown before you dash in.

exceptions.name: Ezreal
exceptions.text: A poke marksman with a blink: Arcane Shift lets him escape all-ins that catch other utility marksmen.

exceptions.name: Tristana
exceptions.text: Both a lane bully and a late carry: she all-ins early with her jump, and her range keeps growing as she levels.

exceptions.name: Kai'Sa
exceptions.text: Scales like a hypercarry but dives like a skirmisher once her ultimate is up.

exceptions.name: Smolder
exceptions.text: Scales from stacks rather than only items, and his slow and ultimate heal help him survive all-ins better than most hypercarries. See the Smolder guide.

exceptions.name: Ziggs
exceptions.text: A mage in Dragon lane: out-ranges and out-clears marksmen early, so play him like a poke lane.

lanes.name: Mid lane
lanes.intro: Mid laners fall into five groups. Mid has no matchup data in the site yet, so these calls are broad and need review.

types.name: Control mages
types.identity: Mid-range area damage and crowd control. They clear waves fast and decide team fights, but struggle once someone gets on top of them.
types.winCondition: Clear waves fast, hold mid priority for your jungler, and save your big area spell for team fights.

types.name: Artillery mages
types.identity: The longest range in the game. Poke from screens away with slow skill shots, but have almost no escape.
types.winCondition: Poke the enemy off the wave and before every objective fight, so your team starts fights with the enemy already low.

types.name: Burst mages
types.identity: Short-range combos that delete one target, often with point-and-click crowd control.
types.winCondition: Land your combo on whoever walks into range, then roam with your lead.

types.name: Assassins
types.identity: Mobile burst that kills squishy targets and escapes. Weak into tanky or crowd-control-heavy lanes.
types.winCondition: Kill or shove your laner, then roam and pick off squishy targets in side lanes.

types.name: Melee skirmishers
types.identity: Melee carries who dash through the wave, sustain and scale. Need the wave to fight.
types.winCondition: Win trades around minions, scale with items, and split-push or flank in fights.

matchups.why: Control mages are immobile, so once an assassin dodges the key skill shot the mage has no escape.
matchups.tip: As the control mage: farm from max range, keep an escape spell or Flash ready, and ask for jungle help early.

matchups.why: Dashes through the wave dodge skill shots, and Yasuo's Wind Wall blocks most control-mage spells.
matchups.tip: As the control mage: shove the wave so there are fewer minions to dash through, and cast after Wind Wall is down.

matchups.why: Point-and-click stuns and burst punish melee champions who have to walk up to farm.
matchups.tip: As the skirmisher: trade only when the stun or cage is on cooldown, and use the wave to dash in from an angle.

matchups.why: Both one-shot each other; whoever lands their combo first wins the trade.
matchups.tip: Track the other combo's cooldowns and only step up when theirs is down.

matchups.why: Control mages out-range burst mages, but burst mages kill them in one combo if they get close.
matchups.tip: As the control mage: keep your distance. As the burst mage: wait in the brush or behind the wave for them to walk up.

matchups.why: Skirmishers' shields and sustain blunt assassin burst, but assassins can still out-roam them.
matchups.tip: As the assassin: don't stay to trade, push and roam. As the skirmisher: punish every roam by taking plates.

matchups.why: Artillery mages out-range control mages, so they can poke them off the wave without stepping into their area spells.
matchups.tip: As the control mage: clear the wave fast so you can step back, and dodge sideways rather than straight back.

matchups.why: Burst mages need to get close to land their combo, and artillery mages poke them down before they can walk into range.
matchups.tip: As the burst mage: wait in the brush or behind the wave, and walk up only after their main poke spell is used.

matchups.why: Artillery mages have slow skill shots and almost no escape, so an assassin who dodges one spell gets a free kill.
matchups.tip: As the artillery mage: stand at max range, keep your crowd-control spell for their engage, and ask your jungler to play mid.

matchups.why: Dashes through the wave dodge slow skill shots, and Yasuo's Wind Wall blocks artillery poke.
matchups.tip: As the artillery mage: shove the wave so there's nothing to dash through, and throw your poke after Wind Wall is down.

exceptions.name: Galio
exceptions.text: A tank mid who reduces incoming magic damage, so he shuts down burst and control mages instead of losing to them.

exceptions.name: Lux
exceptions.text: An artillery mage with a root and a shield, so she can stop an assassin's engage that would kill Vel'Koz or Ziggs.

exceptions.name: Fizz
exceptions.text: An assassin who also beats burst mages: his untargetable hop dodges their key spell.

exceptions.name: Annie
exceptions.text: A burst mage who punishes assassins: her stun stops them halfway through their combo.

exceptions.name: Twisted Fate
exceptions.text: Plays for the map, not the lane: his ultimate lets him join fights anywhere, so he can lose lane and still win the game.

lanes.name: Jungle
lanes.intro: Jungle matchups are about early fights, invades and team fights, not lanes. These calls need review.

types.name: Fighters and divers
types.identity: Strong early duelists who gank often and dive into the back line in fights.
types.winCondition: Invade and gank early, win the first scuttler fights, and snowball your lanes.

types.name: Tanks
types.identity: Engage and crowd control for the team. Slow clear, but hard to kill.
types.winCondition: Set up ganks with crowd control, and start team fights for your carries.

types.name: Assassins
types.identity: Pick off squishy targets and escape. Weak to tanky teams.
types.winCondition: Gank squishy lanes, track the enemy carries, and kill whoever walks out of position.

types.name: Farmers
types.identity: Fast clear and strong late game, but few ganks and weak early fights.
types.winCondition: Clear camps efficiently, take objectives when safe, and carry fights once you have items.

matchups.why: Fighters invade and win early duels, so farmers lose camps and fall behind before they scale.
matchups.tip: As the farmer: ward your jungle entrances, track their start, and clear on the opposite side to avoid them.

matchups.why: Tanks stop auto-attack farmers with crowd control, and their resistances cut farmer damage in fights.
matchups.tip: As the farmer: avoid fighting into their crowd control; take objectives while they gank elsewhere.

matchups.why: Assassins can't one-shot a tank, and tank crowd control locks them down when they dive.
matchups.tip: As the assassin: ignore the tank, flank for the carries, and wait for the tank's engage to be used.

matchups.why: Fighters win early duels, tanks win team fights; the game decides which phase matters.
matchups.tip: As the fighter: use your early lead before tank items arrive. As the tank: avoid early 1v1s.

matchups.why: Both want early fights; fighters duel better, assassins escape better.
matchups.tip: Track the other jungler: invade when they're seen on the opposite side.

matchups.why: Assassins can kill squishy farmers, but farmers out-scale them if the game goes long.
matchups.tip: As the assassin: end before the farmer completes items. As the farmer: stay near your team.

exceptions.name: Rammus
exceptions.text: The tank that hard-counters auto-attack farmers: his taunt and armor turn Master Yi's damage against him.

exceptions.name: Lee Sin
exceptions.text: A fighter who falls off: if he doesn't win early, he's weaker than every other type late.

exceptions.name: Graves
exceptions.text: A farmer who also duels early: his burst makes him dangerous to invade.

exceptions.name: Kayn
exceptions.text: Turns into a fighter or an assassin mid-game depending on the enemy team, so you can't know his type at draft.

lanes.name: Support
lanes.intro: Support types decide how the bot lane plays. These calls are broad and need review.

types.name: Engage tanks
types.identity: Tanky supports who start fights with hard crowd control.
types.winCondition: Look for level 2 all-ins and engage whenever the enemy steps up without an escape.

types.name: Enchanters
types.identity: Heal, shield and speed up their marksman. Win long lanes and long fights.
types.winCondition: Keep your marksman healthy, out-sustain poke, and peel in fights.

types.name: Catchers
types.identity: Hook or pull one target out of position. One good hook wins the lane.
types.winCondition: Stand in the brush, threaten the hook, and punish anyone who walks out from behind minions.

types.name: Mage and artillery supports
types.identity: Long-range poke and area damage, often from artillery mages. Win by chipping the enemy before fights start.
types.winCondition: Poke the enemy off the wave, zone them from farm, and land area spells in fights.

matchups.why: Hard crowd control locks down the squishy enchanter or their marksman before heals and shields matter.
matchups.tip: As the enchanter: stay behind your marksman and save your disengage or shield for their engage.

matchups.why: Long-range poke wears the engage support down before they can get close enough to start a fight.
matchups.tip: As the engage support: hide in brush, wait for their poke spell to be used, then engage.

matchups.why: Heals and shields undo poke, so mage supports run out of mana before they win the lane.
matchups.tip: As the mage support: focus the marksman with full combos instead of chip poke, and look for kills with your jungler.

matchups.why: Most enchanters are immobile and squishy, so one hook on them or their marksman is a kill.
matchups.tip: As the enchanter: stand behind minions and keep your shield for the hooked target.

matchups.why: Mage supports have to step forward to poke, which puts them in hook range.
matchups.tip: As the mage support: poke from behind your minions and only step up when the hook is on cooldown.

matchups.why: Tanky engage supports survive a hook and punish the catcher once the hook is on cooldown.
matchups.tip: As the catcher: hook their marksman, not the tank, and don't throw it when the tank can follow up.

exceptions.name: Morgana
exceptions.text: Her Black Shield blocks crowd control, including hooks, so catchers can't pick her marksman.

exceptions.name: Braum
exceptions.text: An engage tank whose shield blocks projectiles, including hooks and poke, so he beats catchers and mages.

exceptions.name: Janna
exceptions.text: An enchanter who beats engage: her knock-ups and ultimate push all-ins back out.

exceptions.name: Pyke
exceptions.text: A catcher who also executes and roams like an assassin, so he snowballs other lanes too.
